candidates.title: Plcg2 Deficiency Leads to Sex-Associated Divergent Effects on Glial Transcriptomes.
candidates.abstract: Plcg2 encodes an intracellular phospholipase C signaling enzyme expressed predominately in microglia in the brain. Genome-wide association studies implicate PLCG2 in Alzheimer's disease (AD) risk and loss of Plcg2 alters amyloid pathology in mouse models. However, the physiological impact of Plcg2 loss remains unclear. To address this gap, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) of wild-type, heterozygous, and homozygous Plcg2-deficient mouse brains in the absence of amyloid or tau pathology. Our analyses generated a comprehensive, publicly available atlas of glial transcriptomic states across genotypes and sexes. Genotype-associated changes in microglia and astrocytes were enriched in neurodegenerative disease-related pathways, as well as oxidative phosphorylation and proteostasis pathways. Genotype-by-sex interaction and sex-stratified analyses revealed divergent regulation of many of these pathways in males and females, while co-expression and cell-cell communication analyses identified additional sex-associated differences in glial signaling networks. Overall, these data provide a framework for understanding how variation in PLCG2 function may shape glial biology and modify pathways relevant to neurodegenerative disease in a sex-associated manner.

candidates.title: Mesenchymal Stem Cell-Mediated Uptake and Delivery of Indocyanine Green/Doxorubicin-Loaded Stimuli-Responsive Dendrimers to Tumors
candidates.abstract: Abstract Systemic administration of nanocarriers can be limited by rapid clearance and off-target distribution, motivating the investigation of cell-based carrier strategies. Here, we evaluated skin-derived mesenchymal stem cells (S-MSCs) as carriers for PEGylated poly(amidoamine) dendrimer nanoclusters (DNCs) co-loaded with the chemotherapeutic doxorubicin (DOX) and the photothermal dye indocyanine green (ICG). The dendrimer nanoclusters (DNCs-ICG-DOX-PEG) enabled effective co-encapsulation of both cargoes and retained the optical properties required for NIR activation. Confocal imaging confirmed intracellular retention of DOX-associated fluorescence, predominantly within vesicular compartments, for up to 48 h after DNC loading, whereas free DOX was largely lost from S-MSCs within 24 h. At lower tested concentrations, DNC-loading preserved S-MSC metabolic activity, surface marker expression, and migratory function. Irradiation at 808 nm increased DOX release from the DNC formulations and produced an irradiation-dependent reduction in S-MSC metabolic activity. In a pilot murine LLC1 tumor model, S-MSCs preloaded with DNCs and administered adjacent to the tumor were detected within tumor tissue after 24 h, indicating that DNC loading did not abolish local tumor-directed migration. Collectively, these findings demonstrate the feasibility of using S-MSCs as carriers for NIR-responsive, DOX- and ICG-loaded dendrimer nanoclusters and provide a foundation for further studies of cargo biodistribution and therapeutic efficacy.

candidates.title: VEuPathDB: 2026 update on data, tools, and infrastructure for eukaryotic pathogens, vectors, and hosts
candidates.abstract: Abstract The eukaryotic pathogen, vector, and host informatics resource (VEuPathDB, https://veupathdb.org) provides open access to genomic and other large-scale data for protozoan and fungal pathogens, arthropod vectors, and their hosts, supporting >800 organisms and 2602 datasets across 12 component databases, OrthoMCL, and the newly added dataExplorer, as of Release 71 (August 2026). Since our last update, 292 datasets have been integrated, gene product descriptions improved, and OrthoMCL expanded to over 819 000 orthology groups spanning 9.2 million proteins. Artificial intelligence-assisted approaches now support dataset curation, community gene annotation, and experimental summaries of transcriptomic evidence on gene pages, each subject to expert or user review. The new My Datasets workspace lets researchers upload, analyze, and share their own data alongside curated datasets, and a guided interface supports differential expression analysis without programming. Infrastructure has been consolidated from 15 Oracle databases into a single PostgreSQL platform, with data-processing pipelines migrated to containerized Nextflow workflows. This period was also defined by the loss of the long-standing US federal award that funded VEuPathDB, its temporary closure in September 2024, and its restoration under a community-supported model of voluntary tiered subscriptions, donations, and philanthropic support, with all data and tools remaining freely accessible.

candidates.title: Efficacy of acupuncture-related therapies for psoriasis: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (2020–2025)
candidates.abstract: Background Acupuncture-related therapies (ARTs) have been increasingly used for psoriasis, but their comparative efficacy against non-acupuncture interventions remains unclear, and recent evidence lacks systematic synthesis. Methods Nine databases were searched from inception to January 2026, with data extraction limited to 2020–2025. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) on ARTs for psoriasis were included. Traditional pairwise meta-analysis and exploratory network meta-analysis (NMA) were conducted using RevMan, Stata, and RStudio. Primary outcomes were total efficacy rates and Psoriasis Area and Severity Index (PASI) scores. Secondary outcomes included cure rate, Dermatology Life Quality Index (DLQI) scores, pruritus scores, Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) syndrome scores, immune biomarkers, adverse events, and recurrence rates. Heterogeneity, publication bias, subgroup analyses, and meta-regression were systematically explored. Results 35 publications (36 RCTs) involving 3,117 patients and 11 therapies were included. ARTs significantly improved the total efficacy rates (risk ratio [RR] =1.20, 95% CI: 1.16-1.23) and reduced the PASI scores (standardized mean difference [SMD] = -1.55, 95% confidence interval [CI]: -1.83 to -1.28) compared to the controls, with superior effects on all secondary outcomes. The exploratory Surface Under the Cumulative Ranking Curve (SUCRA) ranking for total efficacy rates identified that Acupuncture+Fire Needle was likely the most effective intervention (91.7%), followed by Moving Cupping+Blood-Letting therapy (81.1%) and acupuncture (69.4%). As for PASI score improvement, Moving Cupping+Moxibustion may be ranked highest (95.7%), with Moving Cupping+Blood-Letting therapy (81.2%) and Fire Needle (66.7%) ranking second and third, respectively. Meta-regression showed that intervention types alone moderated the DLQI scores, while intervention types, treatment duration, and psoriasis subtypes moderated the pruritus scores (all P <0.05). No serious adverse events were reported. Conclusions ARTs may benefit patients with psoriasis. However, the evidence is so limited by heterogeneity and incomplete safety reporting that definitive clinical recommendations cannot be made. Systematic review registration https://inplasy.com/ , identifier INPLASY202640100.

candidates.title: Anatomical, physiological, and metabolic trait adjustments in tea leaves under different intercropping systems: implications for ecological tea garden management
candidates.abstract: Introduction Intercropping is widely used to promote sustainable tea cultivation, but how different companion-tree configurations are associated with tea leaf functional traits remains insufficiently understood. This study compared leaf trait responses across four tea-based intercropping systems. Methods A replicated field experiment was conducted in a tea plantation in Zhejiang, China, comparing tea monoculture (CK), tea–persimmon (T+P), tea–pecan (T+H), and tea–persimmon–pecan (T+P+H), with three replicate plots per treatment. Leaf anatomical traits, stomatal density and dimensions, soluble protein, soluble sugars, starch, antioxidant-related indicators, and photosynthetic pigments were measured. Principal component analysis (PCA) was used to summarize multivariate trait variation. Results Intercropping generally reduced epidermal and mesophyll thickness. Relative to CK, T+P had 50.2% lower stomatal density but 32.8% longer and 35.7% wider stomata. It was also associated with 15.1%, 30.1%, and 17.4% higher soluble protein, soluble sugar, and starch concentrations, respectively, 79.6% higher total chlorophyll, and 12.1% lower malondialdehyde (MDA). In contrast, T+P+H showed the greatest mesophyll thinning and the highest MDA concentration. The first two PCA axes explained 55.77% of total trait variation and indicated clear multivariate differentiation between T+P and CK. Discussion These findings indicate that tea-based intercropping configurations are associated with coordinated changes in leaf anatomy, stomatal morphology, metabolism, oxidative status, and pigment profiles. Under the conditions examined, T+P showed the most balanced integrated leaf-trait profile, suggesting its potential for ecological tea-garden management. However, light environment, gas exchange, resource competition, yield, and processed-tea sensory quality were not directly measured, and companion-tree identity was confounded with planting geometry and plot location. The observed responses should therefore be interpreted at the configuration level and validated through multi-season, multi-site studies before broader management recommendations are made.

candidates.title: Codon usage signatures reveal codon-host compatibility trade-offs in the sylvatic-urban cycle of Mayaro virus: implications for urban emergence
candidates.abstract: Introduction Mayaro virus (MAYV) has spilled over into urban mosquito populations, yet the molecular basis of its codon-host compatibility remains unresolved. Methods We analyzed codon usage across 91 complete MAYV genomes, integrating phylogenetic, multivariate and codon-host compatibility analyses. Results Translational selection was the principal force shaping MAYV codon usage: neutrality regression yielded a slope of 0.016 for the full CDS (selection contribution 98.4%), the non-structural region retained a detectable mutational component, and all 91 isolates fell below the ENC-GC3s expectation curve. Among 12 reference species, codon-host compatibility quantified by CAI was highest for the sylvatic vector proxy Sabethes cyaneus (0.808) and lower for urban Aedes vectors and humans (0.743); Sabethes exceeded every urban and human reference after Benjamini–Hochberg correction ( q < 0.001), and this ranking was preserved across NSP and SP partitions, across host strata, and in a human-only consistency check, indicating that it is selection-driven rather than an artifact of sample composition. RCDI and SiD were not concordant and are reported as descriptive divergence measures. RSCU and COA identified CUG and AGA as preferred codons, and CpG/UpA depletion is consistent with immune-mediated selection. Because these indices are computed from reference codon tables, they quantify codon-host compatibility rather than realized fitness. Discussion These findings provide a codon usage baseline for MAYV that may inform codon-deoptimized vaccine design and offer benchmarks for monitoring compatibility with urban vectors as MAYV encounters Aedes populations in the Americas.

candidates.title: Single-molecule whole-genome sequencing reveals genomic and epigenomic concordance between ultrasonic aspiration and surgical resection in meningioma: prospective feasibility series.
candidates.abstract: Background Ultrasonic surgical aspirators, including Sonopet ® , are widely used during skull base meningioma resection to enable safe tumor debulking in constrained corridors, but aspirated tumor fragments are often discarded. Whether this tissue supports genomic and epigenomic profiling comparable to standard resection tissue is unknown. The aim of this study was to determine whether Sonopet ® aspirate is a viable substrate for long-read genomic and epigenomic profiling in skull base meningioma. Methods We prospectively collected paired standard resection (R) and Sonopet ® aspirate (S) specimens from seven patients with skull base meningioma and performed Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) long-read whole-genome sequencing using PromethION R10 flow cells. We compared sequencing yield, read quality, tumor purity, copy-number profiles, somatic single-nucleotide variant (SNV) burden, variant allele frequency, and CpG methylation between matched samples, then projected methylation profiles onto a reference framework of 121 EPIC array-profiled samples for molecular group classification. Results Aspirates generated sequencing yields, read lengths, and tumor purity comparable to matched specimens. Copy-number profiles were largely concordant and recovered canonical meningioma alterations, with close agreement in total and loss burden (Lin's CCC = 0.99, 95% CI 0.76 to 1.00). SNV burden showed moderate agreement (CCC = 0.53, 95% CI - 0.28 to 0.99), with two discordant patients possibly reflecting intratumoral heterogeneity. Promoter methylation was closely correlated between pairs (Pearson r > 0.99 across ~ 177,000 promoters), and molecular group classification was concordant in all pairs except P1, where tumor purity was uncertain. Conclusions Sonopet ® aspirate provides tissue comparable to standard resection specimens for long-read genomic and epigenomic profiling, supporting its use as a substrate for molecular diagnosis and translational research, particularly for subtotally resected tumors with limited tissue.

candidates.title: Immune evasion in Mucorales species: From stealth spores to angioinvasive hyphae
candidates.abstract: Mucormycosis is an invasive fungal infection caused by members of the order Mucorales, which employ stage- and species-specific mechanisms to evade host immunity. Resting spores of experimentally studied Rhizopus species can persist after macrophage uptake because macrophages restrict germination but do not efficiently kill all internalized resting spores. Germination is accompanied by cell-wall remodeling and increased β-glucan exposure in several experimentally examined Mucorales species; however, functional Dectin-1-dependent responses have been demonstrated most clearly in Rhizopus and its conservation across species and isolates remains incompletely defined. Studies predominantly in Rhizopus delemar identify fungal CotH proteins as ligands for host GRP78 or integrin α3β1, linking invasion to tissue-specific host pathways. Intracellular survival also varies across species: Rhizopus spores remain dormant and prevent phagosome maturation, whereas Mucor circinelloides can germinate within macrophages via stress-response and calcineurin-dependent mechanisms. Cunninghamella shows a significant resistance to neutrophil damage, while other Mucorales species suppress accumulation of nitric oxide in activated macrophages. Studies of Rhizopus reveal morphology-dependent dendritic-cell activation and Th17 polarization, and that Rhizopus-specific T cells can directly damage fungal hyphae. Whether such adaptive responses are present in other Mucorales species remains unknown. Understanding these immune evasion mechanisms could support the development of therapies focused on cytokines, adoptive T-cells, and CotH-targets.

candidates.title: Mitochondrial Phylogeny Reveals Deep Intraspecific Divergence and Fine-Scale Regional Structure in Orangutans.
candidates.abstract: Orangutans ( Pongo spp.) are a valuable model for investigating how past climatic and geological events have shaped population structure and species diversification. We reconstructed 237 complete mitochondrial genomes from whole-genome sequencing data and combined them with 50 available mitochondrial sequences, resulting in a dataset of 287 orangutans spanning the current range of Sumatran and Bornean orangutans. Among Sumatran orangutans ( P. abelii ), we identified five geographically distinct mitochondrial clades corresponding to Langkat, North Aceh, Tripa, West Leuser and Batu Ardan. These clades showed strong differentiation, indicating long-term persistence of distinct maternal lineages across the Leuser landscape. For the recently described species, P. tapanuliensis , we added 10 newly reconstructed mitogenomes, increasing representation from 3 to 13 individuals. P. tapanuliensis formed a monophyletic, deeply divergent clade, confirming strong mitochondrial differentiation and long-term isolation. In Bornean orangutans ( P. pygmaeus ), we identified seven major regional mitochondrial clades corresponding to Sarawak, Central Kalimantan, South Kalimantan, Southeast Kalimantan, East Kalimantan and the North and South Kinabatangan populations in Sabah. Within the subspecies P. p. morio , the North and South Kinabatangan, East Kalimantan and Southeast Kalimantan clades formed distinct maternal lineages, revealing substantial mitochondrial structure within the currently recognised subspecies. Our findings suggest that current geographic and taxonomic divisions may under-represent the extent of regional maternal diversity across orangutans. Female philopatry has preserved ancient mitochondrial structure across Sundaland, with its geographic distribution shaped by refugial persistence, major riverine barriers and long-term population fragmentation.

candidates.title: Inbreeding in the genomics era: comparing IBD, drift, and homozygosity-based methods in a pig breeding population.
candidates.abstract: Background The inbreeding and kinship methods can be classified into three approaches: (1) Identity-by-Descent (IBD) estimates the probability that alleles are identical by shared ancestry; (2) Drift-based methods measure deviations in allele frequencies from a base due to genetic drift; and (3) Homozygosity-based (HOM) methods estimate genome-wide homozygosity. The objective of this study was to compare the estimated inbreeding and kinship rates using those three approaches. Within each approach, different methods were investigated. The dataset consisted of purebred sires from artificial insemination centers born between 2014 and 2024, along with their relatives with genotype data, totaling 152,883 pigs. Animals were genotyped with various SNP panels and imputed to medium- and high-density panels (50 K and 660 K). Results For inbreeding estimates, correlations among IBD-based methods were high (0.88), while correlations among drift-based methods ranged from 0.74 to 0.91. Homozygosity-based estimates showed a wide range of correlations (- 0.03 to 1.00). This variability was mainly driven by low or negative correlations involving short runs of homozygosity (ROH) classes (2-4 Mb and 4-8 Mb), which showed poor agreement with longer ROH categories. Correlations between methods from different approaches were generally weak to high (- 0.09 to 0.81). Kinship estimates showed higher correlations than inbreeding estimates. Nevertheless, the same pattern was observed: correlations were consistently higher within the same approach (above 0.96) than across different approaches (above 0.70). Rates of inbreeding and kinship per generation, estimated as regression slopes across birth years and converted to a per-generation scale, were consistently higher for drift-based measures than for the other approaches. This indicates that drift-based and homozygosity-based measures are not equivalent under genomic selection. Their differences are proportional to the covariance between changes in allele frequency and initial allele frequencies. Consequently, minor alleles tend to increase in frequency more often than expected under neutrality in this pig breeding line. Conclusions Overall, the results show that different approaches to estimating inbreeding and kinship convey distinct biological information. Homozygosity-based measures yielded lower estimates than drift-based metrics, suggesting non-neutral dynamics of allele frequencies. These findings indicate that constraining inbreeding using a drift-based genomic relationship matrix within an optimum contribution selection scheme may improve the management of genetic diversity.

candidates.title: Gray bats heighten their response to social cues when navigating group flight in environments with obstacles.
candidates.abstract: Bats are fast fliers with great maneuverability. Many species sense and communicate through echolocation, relying on acoustic signals in the environment. Bats also form large colonies, which necessitates that they fly in groups. When group size increases or obstacles are in their flight paths, the acoustic space can become cluttered, posing a non-trivial challenge for navigation. How do they interact with their environment and conspecifics, and how do they balance social and environmental cues? Recent research has uncovered individual adaptations to calling and flight patterns when flying in the groups or avoiding obstacles. Studies also suggest coordination when foraging, as well as strategies used by the group to mitigate acoustic clutter. However, there has yet to be a study on how bats weigh different navigational tasks when flying in spatially complex environments. Here, we collected stereoscopic video data from a wild colony of gray bats, Myotis grisescens, navigating their usual foraging flight paths in the presence of novel obstacles. We find that bats tend to stay close to a wall, but space out when flying in groups. We develop a data-informed agent-based model which reveals that their social repulsive behavior is strengthened when challenged to navigate novel obstacles.

candidates.title: Explainable machine learning-assisted exploration of chromatin dynamics reveals chromosome-specific response to serum starvation.
candidates.abstract: Chromatin is dynamic at all length scales, influencing chromatin-based processes, such as gene expression. Even large-scale reorganization of whole chromosome territories has been reported upon specific signals, but the lack of suitable methods has prevented analysis of the underlying dynamic processes. Here, we have used CRISPR-Sirius for time-lapse imaging of chromatin loci dynamics during serum starvation. We show that chromosome 1 loci move toward the nuclear envelope during the first hour of serum starvation in a chromosome-specific manner. Machine learning-assisted exploration of acquired multiparametric data combined with the Shapley values-based explanation approach allowed us to uncover the critical features that characterize chromatin dynamics during serum starvation. This analysis reveals that although serum starvation affects overall nuclear morphology and chromatin dynamics, chromosome 1 loci display a specific response that is characterized by maintenance of dynamics in a constrained environment, and long 'jumps' at the nuclear periphery. Interestingly, the two homologous chromosomes display differential behaviors, with the more peripheral homolog being more responsive to the signal than the internal one. Overall, the presented machine learning-assisted dataset exploration helps us navigate the multidimensional data to understand the underlying dynamic processes and can be applied to a wide variety of research questions in imaging and cell biology in general.

candidates.title: Rethinking laboratory sustainability.
candidates.abstract: Green lab initiatives like My Green Lab and LEAF (Laboratory Efficiency Assessment Framework), are paving the way towards sustainable research by promoting resource efficiency, energy conservation, and waste reduction through behavioral changes. However, these initiatives focus almost exclusively on material consumption, overlooking deeper facets of scientific waste that stem from questionable research practices: the environmental cost of unnecessary or poorly designed experiments, discarded null results, unreproducible research, and distorted reporting. I argue that a more meaningful discussion of scientific sustainability must look beyond physical resource management to examine the scientific process itself; to rethink the questions we ask, the experiments we do, and how we communicate our findings. To build a truly sustainable scientific ecosystem, Green Lab initiatives must join forces with Open Science and research integrity movements to update not only the hardware, but also the software of science.

candidates.title: Junctional and actomyosin dynamics drive endothelial cell rearrangements during vascular tube formation.
candidates.abstract: Lumen formation is a key process during the morphogenesis of tubular organs, such as the vertebrate vascular network. At the cellular level, lumen formation can be achieved by cell shape changes or cell rearrangements. We have previously shown that such cell rearrangements are driven by oscillating membrane protrusions, called junction-based lamellipodia (JBL), which provide a ratchet mechanism driving convergent cell movements to connect local lumens, and generate vascular patency. By performing in vivo time-lapse imaging at high spatiotemporal resolution in zebrafish embryos, we have analyzed the cytoskeletal and junctional dynamics, which underlie JBL formation and function. We show that JBL formation requires the activity of the F-actin nucleation complex Arp2/3. We further show that a novel junction is formed at the distal end of the JBL from a pool of VE-cadherin originating from outside the initial JBL area. Subsequently, proximal and distal junctions merge and fuse, a process driven by actomyosin contractility. Prior to this fusion, we observe a specific recruitment of Myl9 within the interjunctional space. Furthermore, inhibition of actomyosin contractility abrogates junctional merging. Taken together, our analyses demonstrate that JBL constitute a module, which, by alternate generation of pushing forces (JBL formation) and pulling forces (junctional merging), provide the physical means for endothelial cells to elongate and to rearrange and thereby generate a continuous vascular lumen.

candidates.title: Diurnal rhythmicity in metabolism and salivary effector expression shapes aphid performance on host plants.
candidates.abstract: Diurnal rhythms influence insect behavior, physiology, and metabolism, optimizing their performance by adapting to daily changes in the environment. While their impact on agricultural pests has been briefly explored, our understanding of how these rhythms drive adaptive responses in pest biology and influence host colonization remains elusive. Here, we show that a notorious global aphid pest, Rhopalosiphum padi , exhibits distinct diurnal patterns in feeding behavior, with elevated honeydew excretion at night and extended phloem salivation during early nighttime. Temporal aphid transcriptome profiling reveals four diurnally rhythmic clusters, two of which peak at night, exhibiting enrichment in carbohydrate and amino acid metabolism. Beyond the established role in manipulating host responses and allowing sustained feeding, our study reveals novel evidence of cyclical fluctuations in salivary effector expression in an insect species. Silencing key effector genes, peaking in expression during the increased nighttime salivation, results in a more pronounced reduction in aphid excretion activity on host plants during the night compared to the day, a phenomenon not observed on artificial diets. A better understanding of aphid diurnal rhythms and their roles in shaping aphid performance provides a promising avenue to refine and optimize pest management, granting a strategic advantage for minimizing crop damage.

candidates.title: Adaptive sampling: information-guided selection for targeted long-read sequencing and epigenetic studies.
candidates.abstract: Adaptive sampling (AS) is a unique feature of nanopore sequencing that enables real-time enrichment or depletion of target molecules during the sequencing run based on their initial sequence information. AS provides a flexible and scalable alternative to conventional capture- and amplification-based approaches, while preserving long reads and the ability to detect epigenetic modifications of native DNA/RNA molecules. In this review, we summarize the principles of AS-based sequencing, explain the enrichment- and depletion-mode strategies and discuss factors affecting its performance. We further highlight the growing body of studies demonstrating the utility of AS across a diverse range of applications, such as metagenomic and microbiome research, structural variant characterization and discovery, studying repeat expansion disorders, integrated genetic and epigenetic profiling or transcriptome analysis. In these and other contexts, AS enables efficient allocation of sequencing capacity toward biologically relevant molecules, while accelerating data generation, which also makes it applicable to rapid molecular diagnostics and real-time genomic analyses in clinical practice. As nanopore sequencing continues to mature and become a standard analysis approach in many laboratories, AS is likely to evolve from a specialized enrichment strategy into a routine component of genomic, epigenomic, and transcriptomic workflows.

candidates.title: GEI-17-mediated SUMOylation of GDP dissociation inhibitor GDI-1 regulates apoptotic cell clearance
candidates.abstract: by Lei Yuan, Peiyao Li, Aiying Ma, Chao Li, Fuqiao Liu, Yunmin Xie, Qian Zheng, Hui Wang, Hui Xiao Apoptotic cell clearance represents the final stage of apoptosis and involves phagosome formation, maturation, and digestion. Here, we found that SUMO modifications participate in apoptotic cell clearance by influencing phagosomal degradation activity in C. elegans . The SUMO E3 ligase, GEI-17, SUMOylates GDP dissociation inhibitor (GDI-1) at K270 to trigger phagosomal degradation. Upon SUMOylation, GDI-1 facilitates release of GDP-bound RAB-1, which is subsequently converted to the GTP-bound form in a manner dependent on GDI displacement factor, PRAF-3. RAB-1 conversion enables binding and translocation of RAB-7 from the endoplasmic reticulum to Golgi to promote phagosome maturation and degradation activity. In the absence of GDI-1 SUMOylation, GDI-1 binds to GDP-RAB-1, sequestering it in the cytoplasm, resulting in impaired phagosomal degradation. Furthermore, we found SUMOylation of GDI1 at a conserved site plays a crucial role in efferocytosis regulation in mammals. This study defines a previously unrecognized mechanism by which SUMOylation drives apoptotic cell clearance.

candidates.title: Local feedback governs cell fate transition to drive self-organized phenotypic equilibrium in hierarchical tumors
candidates.abstract: by Emma Legait, Charlotte Rulquin, Lauranne Bouteille, Raphaël Clément, Cédric Maurange How cell-state transitions are regulated along a tumor lineage to determine its overall cellular composition remains unclear. Using a simple hierarchical tumor model in Drosophila , we show that differentiation of cancer stem cells (CSCs) into transit amplifying progenitors (TAPs) depends on the fraction of TAPs among their immediate neighbors. This relationship is captured by a local feedback transition rule that quantitatively predicts CSC transition probability. Implementing this rule in 3D growth simulations spontaneously recapitulates CSC clustering and the emergence of a stable CSC fraction within tumors. Mechanistically, the local feedback is mediated by EGFR signaling from newly produced TAPs, propagating differentiation across CSC clusters. Consistently, we show that clustering protects the CSC pool from depletion driven by surrounding TAPs, indicating that spatial architecture and lineage dynamics are tightly coupled. Together, these findings show that a local feedback governing fate transitions drives emergent spatial organization that stabilizes the stem cell fraction in hierarchical tumors.

candidates.title: Migration as a key influence on ungulate eco-evolutionary history
candidates.abstract: by Gustavo Burin Species can overcome resource limitations by migrating to more favourable areas. A new study in PLOS Biology shows that migration has an important effect on the diversification dynamics of ungulates, that likely led to changes in ecosystem functioning. Species can overcome environmental limitations by migrating to more favorable areas. This Primer explores a new study in PLOS Biology showing that this behavior has an important effect on the diversification dynamics of ungulates, which in turn likely led to changes in ecosystem properties and functioning.

candidates.title: An indirect wing steering muscle stabilizes flight by regulating wing pitch angle in Drosophila
candidates.abstract: by Han Kheng Teoh, Debojyoti Biswas, Haoru Li, Abby Leung, B. Kemper Ludlow, Samuel C. Whitehead, Erica Ehrhardt, Michael Dickinson, Tsevi Beatus, Noah J. Cowan, Itai Cohen Flapping flight is inherently unstable, requiring Drosophila to fine-tune their wing motions on a milliseconds timescale. Pioneering studies have shown that the direct steering muscles, which attach to the wing hinge, are important for generating these rapid flight reflexes. Recent connectome data, however, reveal that indirect steering muscles or tension muscles, which alter the mechanics of the thorax, receive some of the same synaptic inputs from the sensory apparatus as the direct steering muscles. This discovery suggests that the indirect steering muscles may also be important for flight control. Here, we show that the indirect tergopleural muscles indeed contribute substantially to stabilization, particularly for large pitch perturbations. We find that for small perturbations (less than 1,000 °/s), flies modulate their wing stroke amplitude to generate lift-based corrective torques, a strategy that has been previously documented. For larger perturbations, however, we observe that Drosophila engage an additional wing degree of freedom—the wing pitch angle—to leverage additional lift and drag forces during the corrective maneuver. Quasi-steady aerodynamic simulations reveal that this strategy minimizes power consumption, anaolgous to how some mammals (including humans) adjust their steady-state gaits in a near energy-optimal manner. Using optogenetics and a control theory framework, we demonstrate that the tergopleural muscle is activated by a proportional gain component of a nonlinear proportional-integral controller responsible for determining the wing pitch angle during large perturbations. A simplified torsional spring model for the wing hinge captures the changes in the wing pitch dynamics observed during correction maneuvers by using the tergopleural muscle to adjust the rest angle of the wing. These findings provide a striking example of reflex strategy selection in time-critical behaviors and underscore the vital role of indirect steering muscles in flight stabilization.

candidates.title: Dynamic functional connectivity reveals evolving neural activity states of alcohol-seeking in rats
candidates.abstract: by Yujing Zhang, Nicholas M. Timme, Mintao Liu, Christopher C. Lapish, Joaquín Goñi The brain mechanisms underlying persistent alcohol-seeking in Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD) remain incompletely understood. To investigate this behavior, we characterized the temporal evolution of neural activity states in the anterior cingulate cortex of freely behaving rats performing an aversion-resistant drinking (ARD) task. Alcohol-preferring (P) rats were assessed, as they reliably exhibit ARD when alcohol is devalued with the bitter tastant quinine. P rats were compared with Wistar rats, which progress slower to ARD, as indicated by cessation of drinking following quinine devaluation. Using dynamic functional connectivity analyses of spike-train recordings, we identified latent neural states corresponding to seeking and non-seeking phases. We then integrated the latent-state decoding of neural activity with a seeking intensity model derived from the observed drinking behavior. This framework revealed that the decoded latent neural states closely tracked behavior. Furthermore, during alcohol-reinforced sessions, neural and behavioral measures of drinking or non-drinking states were strongly aligned in both strains. However, after alcohol devaluation, this alignment diverged in P rats but remained consistent in Wistars. The inability of P rats to acquire stable neural states following devaluation suggests impaired formation of latent states as a neural mechanism of ARD, offering insights into the cognitive vulnerabilities that may sustain AUD.

candidates.title: Allosteric inhibition rescues hydrocephalus caused by catalytically inactive Shp2 in mice
candidates.abstract: by Neoklis Makrides, Emily Sun, Hilal Mir, Jen-Zen Chuang, Ziyuan Jiang, Yihua Wu, Carlos Serra, John Peregrin, Qian Wang, Wellington V. Cardoso, Ching-Hwa Sung, Neel H. Shah, Xin Zhang SHP2, a protein tyrosine phosphatase (PTP) crucial in Ras-MAPK signaling, is associated with various human congenital diseases and cancers. Here, we show that the catalytically inactive Shp2 C459S mutation results in communicating hydrocephalus, similar to the catalytically activating Shp2 E76K and Mek1 DD mutants. Unlike previous mutants, however, Shp2 C459S/+ mutation uniquely affects ciliary development rather than neurogenesis, leading to structural abnormalities in cilia and impaired ciliary motility. Differential scanning fluorimetry suggested that SHP2 C459S , SHP2 E76K , and SHP2 C459S/E76K mutations all induce an open SHP2 conformation, but only SHP2 C459S leads to aberrant GAB1 phosphorylation in cells expressing wild-type SHP2. Consistent with this distinct signaling profile, brain ventricular tissues from Shp2 C459S/+ mice exhibit elevated GAB1 and AKT phosphorylation despite normal ERK and STAT3 activities, implicating dysregulated PI3K–AKT signaling in the pathogenesis of hydrocephalus. Importantly, pharmacological inhibition of PI3K markedly rescues ciliogenesis defects and alleviates hydrocephalus in mutant mice. Furthermore, the allosteric SHP2 inhibitor SHP099 increases the thermal stability of SHP2C459S protein, consistent with a shift toward a closed state, and ameliorates hydrocephalus in Shp2 C459S/+ mice. These findings suggest that, in this engineered mouse model, Shp2 -associated hydrocephalus is driven by conformational changes rather than altered catalytic activity. Our results underscore the therapeutic potential of conformation-specific allosteric inhibitors in targeting both catalytically active and inactive SHP2 mutants.

candidates.title: A Unified Framework for Self-Recognition Across Monkeys, Infants, and Robots
candidates.abstract: Self-recognition is a basic cognitive ability that indicates self-consciousness in humans. However, whether non-human agents such as monkeys and robots can possess a similar sense of self remains debated. Here, we develop a multi-scenario apparatus to examine self-recognition from different perspectives across macaque monkeys, human infants, and simulated robots. Monkeys trained for mirror-perspective (MP) self-face recognition were able to spontaneously recognize themselves when viewing video images of their back from a third-person perspective (3PP); however, this generalization required a few minutes of "exploration". In contrast, monkeys trained for 3PP self-back recognition spontaneously demonstrated MP self-recognition within seconds. Meanwhile, first-person-perspective (1PP) self-hand recognition represented a more basic ability that naive monkeys could achieve naturally. Interestingly, human infants aged 1 to 2 years exhibited a stepwise developmental sequence of 1PP, MP, and 3PP self-recognition abilities, consistent with the hierarchical levels of self-recognition in monkeys. Furthermore, we constructed world-model-based simulated robots and found that robots equipped with a body schema exhibited the emergence of self-recognition ability following multisensory integration training, along with the spontaneous generalization of self-recognition across different perspectives. Notably, the formation of internal self-body maps was identified as a key factor enabling this generalization. The convergence of findings across humans, monkeys, and robots not only redefines the evolutionary continuity of the self but also provides an operational framework for designing artificial systems capable of locating themselves in the world.

candidates.title: Emerging transient dynamics at finite observation scales
candidates.abstract: Biogeochemical, ecological, and astronomical systems are transient. Yet, predicting dynamical shifts remains challenging because of inferential uncertainties in datasets and the limitations of asymptotic-dependent theories. To address this problem, we developed a theoretical framework that builds on the finite nature of observations. This framework assesses the relative importance of processes, defined as the mechanisms that contribute to the rate of change of the system's dynamic variables; this allows prediction of switching thresholds, that is, the values of the dynamic variables at which a process becomes relevant or irrelevant, switching the dynamics into a new dynamic regime. The framework predicts that the number of possible observable dynamic regimes increases exponentially with the number of processes. Yet observers are expected to experience only a subset of those dynamic regimes, determined by which processes remain relevant throughout the observation. The framework was tested on a case study of a classic predator-prey system comprising four processes parameterized for bacteria (prey) and lytic bacteriophages (predator). The analysis recovered the sixteen dynamic regimes predicted by the framework, including two non-trivial quasi-equilibrium dynamics. The classical quasi-equilibrium solution, with all processes being relevant, was observed in only about one in ten simulated trajectories that covered the observational window. An adaptive Boolean model, using only relevant observable processes, validated the framework's accuracy by recovering the full model's dynamics within the observer's tolerance. The observational framework introduced here provides a strategy for identifying the processes and conditions that lead to significant switches in dynamic regimes. The framework complements asymptotic approaches to transient dynamics by focusing on the observer's specific, finite context rather than the system's asymptotic states. It can also guide experimental design to measure a process's impact in a dynamical system and suggests actions to suppress it.

candidates.title: The activation-deactivation cycle of human PIEZO1
candidates.abstract: PIEZO1 is a cation channel that is primarily activated through mechanical force, and activation has been shown to be influenced by membrane curvature. PIEZO1 is ubiquitously expressed and plays critical roles in various patho-/physiological processes such as inflammatory diseases or red blood cell volume regulation. Here we combine coarse-grained and atomistic simulations in which human PIEZO1 is embedded in a curved membrane and subjected to simulations under controlled membrane tension and a physiological transmembrane potential, allowing the gating cycle to be reconstructed at atomic resolution. Systematic pressure adaptation identifies an activation regime in which the channel flattens progressively, and ion permeation quantitatively reproduces the experimental conductance of 36 pS. Furthermore, the R2456-E2117 salt bridge couples pore lipid retention to the anchor domain and disrupting it reproduces the phenotypes of the disease-associated R2456H and R2456C variants. PIEZO activation is transmitted through an interconnected network of contact rearrangements that ultimately reshapes the yoda1 binding pocket at the THU8/THU9 interface. This state-dependent remodelling rationalises the pharmacology of yoda1 and offers a framework for the structure-based design of PIEZO1 modulators.

candidates.title: Insulin signaling in pericytes is a master regulator of endocrine and vascular niches in pancreatic islets
candidates.abstract: Insulin plays a crucial role in lowering glycemia, but it is also a powerful anabolic hormone with potent effects on the vasculature. Most studies on insulin vascular actions have focused on endothelial cells. Much less is known about its effects on the mural cells of the microvasculature known as pericytes. This gap in knowledge is particularly relevant for the pancreatic islet microvasculature which is exposed to high insulin levels and relies on local pericytes to efficiently deliver its glucoregulatory hormones. To investigate how insulin affects islet pericyte function and the impact on glucose homeostasis, we generated mice that lack insulin receptors in pericytes (PerIRKO). Loss of insulin signaling in pericytes raised insulin levels, induced islet expansion and beta cell proliferation in the pancreas and in intraocular islet grafts from PerIRKO mice. These changes in beta cell numbers were accompanied by increased islet vascular density, although capillaries were dysfunctional ex vivo, compromising islet hormonal responses to an intravenous glucose challenge. Our study supports that insulin itself regulates islet endocrine and vascular niches through previously unrecognized actions on pericytes, revealing a novel mechanism that links the vasculature to endocrine homeostasis.

candidates.title: Cerebellar transcranial AC stimulation produces frequency and phase-dependent changes in Purkinje cell complex spike waveform
candidates.abstract: Cerebellar transcranial alternating current stimulation (ctACS) can improve motor learning and may speed rehabilitation. The mechanisms by which ctACS induces long-term changes in brain function that underlie these effects are not known, and knowledge of them could greatly improve the application of ctACS. One potential mechanism is alteration of Purkinje cell (PC) complex spike (CS) activity, as CS activity is a key regulator of cerebellar synaptic plasticity. Thus, we investigated how ctACS modifies CS firing rates and waveform. Extracellular recordings were obtained from cerebellar PCs in anesthetized adult rats while ctACS (250 A) was applied across a range of frequencies (0.5 - 50 Hz). The effect of ctACS on CS waveform was quantified via measuring changes in the overall size of the CS and in the number and amplitude of the spikelets that comprise a CS. ctACS produced phase-dependent modulation of the CS waveform in a majority of PCs at most tested frequencies, with 1 Hz stimulation causing modulation in all PCs tested at the frequency. The modulation reflected changes within the normal range of CS waveforms rather than an expansion of that range. Analysis of individual spikelet periods (windows) revealed that ctACS modified discrete portions of the CS, with 93.8% of PCs showing significant modulation in at least one window. Notably, the strength of phase-dependent CS waveform modulation was relatively consistent across frequencies, in contrast to the frequency dependence of simple spike (SS) entrainment. Significant modulation of spikelet amplitude was found more often than that of spikelet number; however, the relative strength of the modulation when present was similar for the two parameters. CS waveform modulation was correlated with SS entrainment strength and was strongest in PCs located near the cerebellar surface (i.e., near the apices of the folia). Together, these findings demonstrate that ctACS exerts phase-dependent control over CS waveform. Moreover, the differing frequency dependence of the waveform effects and SS firing modulation suggests that it may be possible to target CS-related plasticity selectively, providing a potential strategy for selectively modulating cerebellar learning with ctACS.

candidates.title: Variable penetrance of schizophrenia in 22q11.2 deletion syndrome is associated with impaired, but reversible, neuronal mitophagy.
candidates.abstract: The 22q11.2 deletion syndrome (22qDS) is a major genetic risk factor for schizophrenia (Sz). We found that iPSC-derived neurons (iNeurons) from 22qDS +Sz individuals exhibit weaker mitochondrial energetics, whereas iNeurons from individuals with the same deletion but no psychosis (22qDS -Sz) upregulate expression of mitochondrial biogenesis-related genes. Here, we investigated why the +Sz group fails to undergo this compensation, finding that 22qDS +Sz iNeurons have older and more depolarized mitochondria than 22qDS -Sz or controls. Transcriptomic and proteomic analyses revealed downregulation of mitophagy-related pathways, and live imaging revealed elevated lysosomal pH. Restoring lysosomal acidity with acidifying nanoparticles improved mitophagy and, remarkably, increased the expression of mitochondrial biogenesis-related transcription factors in the +Sz neurons. We conclude that lysosomal dysfunction and impaired mitophagy differentiate 22qDS individuals who develop schizophrenia from those who do not. Mitophagy could be a novel therapeutic or preventative opportunity for Sz in the context of genetic neurodevelopmental disorders.

candidates.title: Polaris: A toolkit for standardized construction, integration, and quantitative testing in Escherichia coli and Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
candidates.abstract: Existing synthetic biology toolkits have expanded part libraries and assembly capabilities. However, new users may still encounter ambiguity in construct definitions, hierarchical transitions, genomic integration routes, and quantitative testing procedures. Here, we present Polaris, a Golden Gate toolkit for Escherichia coli and Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Polaris uses a MoClo-derived three-level hierarchy. Level 1 stores reusable parts, Level 2 generates transcription units and other intermediate constructs, and Level 3 supports multigene assembly and switching between testing and integration backbones. The toolkit distinguishes part interfaces from transcription unit interfaces, uses BpiI and BsaI in successive assembly stages, and provides parallel ccdB and mScarletI3 screening options. Integration modules and quantitative characterization frameworks were implemented in both hosts and demonstrated using representative genetic parts and activation and repression systems. A companion digital platform further encodes the Level 1 to Level 3 rules for assembly planning. Polaris connects hierarchical construction, stable genetic implementation, and quantitative testing within a common execution framework, providing a practical basis for data accumulation, part standardization, and future automation.

candidates.title: Genetic and environmental predictors of seasonality and seasonal affective disorder in individuals with depression.
candidates.abstract: The etiology and nosological status of seasonal affective disorder (SAD) as a specifier of depressive episodes versus a transdiagnostic disorder are the subject of debate. In this study, we investigated the underlying etiology of SAD and dimensional seasonality by examining their association with latitude and genetic risk for a range of traits, and investigated gene-environment interactions. This study included 12,460 adults (76% female, aged 18-90) with a history of depression from the Australian Genetics of Depression Study. Regression models included predictors for latitude (distance from equator) and polygenic scores for eight traits: major depressive disorder, bipolar disorder, anxiety disorders, chronotype, sleep duration, body mass index, vitamin D levels, and educational attainment. Outcomes were SAD status and general seasonality score. SAD was positively associated with latitude (OR[95%CI] = 1.05[1.03-1.06], padjusted < 0.001), and there was nominal evidence of additive and multiplicative interactions between chronotype genetic risk and latitude (β = -0.0014[-0.0024,-0.0003], padjusted = 0.122; OR = 0.98[0.97-1.00], padjusted = 0.122). General seasonality score was associated with latitude (IRR = 1.01[1.01-1.01], padjusted < 0.001) and genetic risk for major depressive disorder (IRR =1.03[1.02-1.04], padjusted < 0.001), bipolar disorder (IRR = 1.02[1.01-1.03], padjusted = 0.001), anxiety disorders (IRR = 1.03[1.01-1.04], padjusted < 0.001), vitamin D levels (OR = 0.89[0.83-0.96], padjusted = 0.048), and educational attainment (IRR = 0.97[0.96-0.98], padjusted < 0.001). These findings enhance understanding of SAD etiology, highlighting contributions of psychiatric genetic risk and geographic measures on seasonal behavior, and support examining seasonality as a continuous dimension.

candidates.title: Characterizing hypertension in activated PI3K delta syndrome: Findings from Epic Cosmos.
candidates.abstract: APDS is a rare inborn error of immunity with comorbidity patterns that have yet to be characterized at a large scale. Using Epic Cosmos, a de-identified electronic health record database, we conducted a retrospective, cross-sectional analysis of 866 patients identified by structured diagnosis codes (ICD-10: D84.81; SNOMED: 793412000). Findings revealed that hypertension was coded as affecting 28.5% of the cohort, with age-stratified analyses demonstrating higher prevalence among younger APDS patients compared with age-matched non-APDS peers. Among patients aged ≤50 years, hypertension prevalence was 24.05% in the APDS group compared with 10.89% in the age-matched non-APDS population (prevalence ratio 2.21, 95% CI, 1.90-2.57, P < 0.0001). This association remained prominent in a more specific APDS sensitivity cohort in which the base population required an APDS diagnosis, alongside an allergy and immunology encounter. The findings of this paper provide large-scale characterization of APDS and identify hypertension, particularly among younger APDS patients, as a potentially underrecognized comorbidity that warrants further investigation.

candidates.title: Getting by "With a Little Help From My Friends": Collegial and peer support in allergy-immunology.
candidates.abstract: Health care professionals face many challenges in practice for which collegial and peer support can be impactful. Some of the most seemingly insurmountable struggles result from medical error or an adverse patient outcome. Clinicians may experience remorse, guilt, sadness, burnout, depression, and isolation, potentially causing second victim syndrome. In addition, medical professionals face daily frustrations due to loss of clinical autonomy, operational pressures, shrinking margins, workforce shortages, misaligned institutional incentives, and corporatization of health systems that can lead to burnout and moral injury. It is therefore critically important to support clinicians and ensure that those who dedicate their lives to caring for others feel heard, have a safe and supportive sounding board to debrief stressful situations, and do not feel abandoned. Collegial networks and peer support are important and helpful resources. This article reviews key aspects of collegial and peer support programs that can benefit health care professionals in allergy-immunology and beyond.
candidates.journal: The journal of allergy and clinical immunology. Global

candidates.title: Reprogramming tumor vasculature: Integrating normalization biology with vascularized tumor-on-chip models.
candidates.abstract: Abnormal tumor vasculature is a hallmark of the tumor microenvironment that promotes hypoxia, therapeutic resistance, and disease progression while limiting the delivery of anticancer therapy. Although early anti-angiogenic therapies were designed to starve tumors by eliminating their blood supply, excessive vessel pruning often aggravated hypoxia and selected for more aggressive phenotypes. These observations led to the concept of vascular normalization, whereby judicious modulation of angiogenic signaling transiently restores vessel structure and function, improving perfusion, oxygenation, drug delivery, and anti-tumor immunity. In this review, we discuss the mechanisms governing tumor vessel formation, maturation, and dysfunction, and examine therapeutic strategies aimed at normalizing the tumor vasculature. We further highlight the major challenges limiting clinical translation, including the transient and heterogeneous nature of the normalization window, adaptive resistance mechanisms, and the lack of robust tools for longitudinal monitoring. We then integrate vascular normalization biology with vascularized tumor-on-chip platforms, examining how key features of the tumor microenvironment, including tissue architecture, extracellular matrix remodeling, hemodynamic forces, metabolic gradients, and multicellular interactions, can be recreated and quantitatively monitored. We critically evaluate how engineering design, biomaterial selection, vascularization strategies, perfusion, and integrated sensing influence the ability of these platforms to capture vascular normalization and therapeutic responses. By linking the hallmarks of vascular normalization to measurable on-chip phenotypes, vascularized tumor-on-chip systems provide controlled frameworks for investigating resistance mechanisms, optimizing treatment timing, and advancing precision oncology. However, challenges related to physiological fidelity, standardization, scalability, and clinical validation continue to limit their broader translation.

candidates.title: Plug-and-Play or Plug-and-Pray? Impact of random versus targeted integration on the linearity and orthogonality of synthetic gene circuits in CHO cells.
candidates.abstract: Predictable and tuneable gene expression is essential for advanced mammalian cell engineering yet remains challenged by genomic position effects and copy number variability. This study systematically compares random integration (RI) and targeted integration (TI) of two synthetic lineariser gene circuits, TetR/eGFP_Lin and PhlFd/mCherry_Lin, in CHO-S cells. Both circuits exhibited strong linearity and orthogonality across integration strategies, but integration method and repressor choice produced distinct performance trade-offs. RI increased achievable dynamic range for PhlFd but increased basal leakiness for TetR, whereas TI, via a dual-landing-pad system, constrained copy number, and reduced basal expression and PhlFd expression variability. These findings highlight integration context and circuit architecture as key design parameters informing rational design of synthetic regulators for biopharmaceutical applications.

candidates.title: RiboMeth-Sequencing Reveals Selective Ribosomal RNA 2'-O-Methylation Changes in the Dorsolateral Prefrontal Cortex of Subjects With Major Depressive Disorder.
candidates.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is associated with widespread molecular abnormalities in the brain; however, the contribution of ribosome-centered regulatory mechanisms remains poorly understood. Ribosomal RNA (rRNA) 2'-O-methylation (Nm) is the most abundant and evolutionarily conserved RNA modification and has emerged as a determinant of ribosome heterogeneity and translational control. However, the rRNA Nm landscape has not been examined in psychiatric illness. Here, we used RiboMeth-seq to map site-specific rRNA Nm in the MDD brain. RiboMeth-seq was performed in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex of individuals with MDD (n = 17) and matched nonpsychiatric control subjects (n = 20) using an Illumina NextSeq2000 in 50-bp single-end mode. Specific RiboMeth-seq scores were calculated in ±2 nucleotide intervals for all RNA positions and extracted for the positions of known Nm residues in target RNA. The overall distribution of ribose methylation scores was highly similar between groups, indicating the preservation of the global rRNA Nm landscape in MDD. At the same time, we identified 8 significantly altered Nm sites, including 4 in 28S rRNA (Am2802, Cm2848, Cm3866, and Gm4593) and 4 in 18S rRNA (Um172, Am576, Am1031, and Gm1490). These selective changes occurred in the absence of widespread remodeling, supporting a model in which MDD is associated with targeted modification of functionally relevant ribosomal positions rather than a generalized disruption of ribosome integrity. Our findings identify rRNA Nm as a previously unrecognized layer of molecular alteration in MDD and suggest that site-specific variation in ribosome composition may contribute to aberrant translational regulation in the depressed brain.
